paragraphs: I'm writing to apply for the .NET CMS Tech Lead role at MicroSourcing. As a Senior Developer currently leading technical delivery on enterprise .NET systems for a New Zealand insurance provider, I'm used to owning solution architecture end-to-end while guiding the engineers around me toward it.

At Delta Insurance, I provide technical governance and quality assurance by reviewing the architectural and code contributions of peer Senior Developers, driving development, support, and release execution across two core systems: a legacy .NET Framework application and a modern 5-microservice .NET Core backend with a React frontend. Outside that role, I directed the end-to-end digital transformation of a higher-education client, designing three interconnected systems and migrating them onto a secure, cloud-native AWS infrastructure with automated CI/CD — the kind of solution architecture and client-facing technical ownership this role calls for.

I haven't worked directly with Sitecore, Kentico, or Optimizely, but my background is squarely in the enterprise ASP.NET Core architecture, RESTful API design, and Azure/AWS cloud delivery that sit underneath CMS platforms like these, and I pick up new platform-specific tooling quickly.
I'd welcome the chance to talk through how my governance and delivery experience could apply to your client engagements. Thank you for your consideration.
